audit.whatIsWrong: All seven chart rows disagree between layers. Full: Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill/Yone/Skill/Yone. Content: Akshan/Akshan/Akshan/Akshan/Akshan/Yone/Akshan.
audit.why: At 55.16% over 2547 games Akshan genuinely wins the early lane — a 450-range melee with no ranged tool walks into an 850 boomerang. Level 6 belongs to Yone (Fate Sealed), first item is even, and late Yone chooses the fight.
audit.corrected: Akshan / Akshan / Akshan / Akshan / Yone / Skill / Yone, proposed as one atomic group across both layers.

audit.whatIsWrong: The first-item spike claimed Akshan out-trades Yone in extended fights, and the late spike claimed Comeuppance 'erases his flanks'.
audit.why: Spirit Cleave shields on a 14-second cooldown that shortens with his attack speed, so extended trades are exactly what his items buy. Fate Sealed falls to 80 seconds and has 1000 range, so late he chooses the engage — Comeuppance is a reactive answer after he lands, not a deterrent to his approach.
audit.corrected: Level 6 and late are Yone's spikes; Akshan's are levels 3-5 and, at parity, first item.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page treats Soul Unbound (E) as Yone's dash and gap-closer — 'walk his E through your zone', 'every dash he commits to', 'his only gap closer is that same E'. It also invents an 'Avengerang mark' and calls W a poke tool.
audit.why: Soul Unbound sends Yone's spirit out while his body stays behind; when it ends he is forced back to the body and repeats part of the damage. It closes no gap on you. His actual gap-closes are the two-stack Mortal Steel knockup dash (450) and Fate Sealed (1000). Akshan's Q leaves no mark and his W is camouflage, not poke.
audit.corrected: Punish the two-stack Mortal Steel step-up; treat Soul Unbound as a 22-second damage window that ends by snapping him back, not as an approach.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'take the fifteen-second invitation' for a spent Soul Unbound.
audit.why: Soul Unbound is 22/19/16/13/10 — fifteen seconds is not any rank of it.

edits.before: Once you finish your first item spike you out-trade his Steraks/PD rush in extended fights since your passive stacks punish every dash-in he commits to.
edits.after: Your first item lands about when his does, and Spirit Cleave shields on a 14-second cooldown that shortens with his attack speed — do not extend.

edits.before: Comeuppance lets you erase Yone's flanks in teamfights, turning his own dive angle into a death sentence.
edits.after: Late, Fate Sealed is 80 seconds and reaches 1000 range — save Comeuppance for after he lands, not the approach.

edits.before: Yone has to walk his E through your Avengerang zone to reach you, and every dash he commits to eats a free auto plus Q proc from your passive. You can zone him off caster minions with Heroic Swing angles he can't easily punish, since his only gap closer is that same E. Play patient poke — he has no ranged pressure of his own pre-6, so short trades favor you almost every time.
edits.after: Yone has to walk 450 range into your 850 boomerang, and his only gap-close is the two-stack Mortal Steel knockup — Soul Unbound is a spirit that snaps back to his body, not a dash at you. Zone him off the caster minions with swing angles, and trade on every wave contact: he has no ranged pressure at all before 6, so short trades are free damage.

edits.before: Lvl 6 flips briefly in Yone's favor: Fate Sealed pulls you together with his allies and his crit-scaling burst can catch you before your R is back up if you got baited into a bad position. Play around wards and vision on his jungler here, and don't contest him in a vacuum — bring your R off cooldown before you commit to a fight. From Lvl 7 on your resets and repeated poke put you back ahead, especially if you can catch his E on cooldown.
edits.after: Level 6 flips to Yone: Fate Sealed blinks behind the last champion in a 1000-range line and pulls everyone it hit back to him, and his crit burst finishes the pull while your R is still on 100 seconds. Play the vision game and never contest him in a vacuum. From 7 on, repeated poke puts you back level — Soul Unbound is 22 seconds at rank 1 and is a spirit swap, not a gap-close, so the window after it ends is yours.

edits.before: By first item you consistently punish his dashes with passive burst, and your R turns his own flanking habit into free picks in teamfights. Play the disengage game — Heroic Swing to peel or reposition, then execute overextended dives with Comeuppance. As long as you don't facecheck his flank angle blind, he can't reliably close the gap on you late.
edits.after: Late, Fate Sealed is 80 seconds and reaches from 1000 range, so he picks the moment, not you. Play disengage: Heroic Swing to peel or reposition, and hold Comeuppance for after he lands rather than for his approach. Keep vision on the flank angle — the fight you lose is the one that starts on top of you with your swing already spent.

notes: The whole page was built on Soul Unbound being Yone's gap-closing dash. It is not — the spirit leaves his body and is forced back to it, closing no distance on you; his gap-closes are the two-stack Mortal Steel knockup (450) and Fate Sealed (1000). That error drove the trade advice, the wants, the early text and the focus field. It also invented an 'Avengerang mark' and treated Akshan's W as poke when it is camouflage. Chart disagreed on all seven rows between layers and is now proposed as one atomic group: Akshan 1-3 and 4-5, Yone at 6, Skill at first item, Yone at 2+ items. NOTE: focus.text still reads 'Yone Soul Unbound' and the matchup's real focus is Fate Sealed, but that string is 17 characters and the applier skips anything under 25, so I have not proposed it — it needs a manual change, and it also feeds breakdown.cooldowns, loading and report[5]. win[0] appears in the edit list with an unchanged value only to keep the chart group complete; drop it if the applier objects.
